Subject: MAP kickoff: intro, roles, and eval dry‑run — calendar & tech checks

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to get a short MAP kickoff on the calendar to align stakeholders, confirm the evaluation plan, and run a quick tech dry‑run so the evaluation environment is ready when your team starts tokenized tests next week.

Proposed logistics (please confirm):
- Duration: 60 minutes
- Date/time (PT): Apr 30, 2027 10:00–11:00 AM PT
- Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/999888777?pwd=dryrun (passcode: nxgMAP)

Draft agenda (attached: MAP_Agenda_v1.pdf):
1) Introductions & roles (10m) — who is owning each MAP stream
2) Evaluation plan overview + success criteria (15m) — dataset slices, pass/fail gates
3) Tech dry‑run (20m) — credentialing, data flow, sample prompt run
4) Next steps, timelines & owner commitments (15m)

Who from your side will join? We suggest: product owner, security/compliance lead, and one engineer who will run the evals. I’ve attached a stakeholder roster template (Stakeholder_Roster.csv) you can fill and return.

If Apr 30 doesn’t work, we can shift to May 3 or May 4 morning PT — tell me what works and I’ll send an updated invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555‑0123

- Can your team provide a small example dataset and a short list of prompts you’ll use for the test run (so we can validate data handling and PII rules)?

1) Example dataset & prompts- We’ll post a small sanitized sample (CSV, ~200 rows) and the prompt set to a temporary secure link by EOD Friday. That will include a README describing which columns are required for the eval harness.

2) Network allowlist- For the dry‑run you only need to allow the following egress IPs: 34.201.12.45, 34.201.12.46 (these are temporary test endpoints). For production we’ll provide the official list via the security questionnaire but those two are enough for the session.

3) Roles — tentative owners: 
- Sofia Ivanova (Redwood) — MAP lead, agenda & followups
- Marcus Lin (Redwood) — eval harness & data prep
- Lauren Bishop (Redwood) — success criteria, QA metrics
- Ben Carter (Redwood) — runtime configuration & SLOs
- Alex Brown (NexGen) — product owner / final approver
- Jordan Ellis (NexGen) — integration engineer (runs the sample prompts)
- Priya Kapoor (NexGen) — security/compliance reviewer

I’ve pushed an updated agenda to the Zoom invite and attached the two files above.

If everyone confirms, I’ll send a final calendar invite with the attendee list and a short runbook (where to drop the sample file during the call).

Best,
Sofia
